rationale: Stiven brings deep technical expertise in AI, computer vision, and embedded systems to build regulated medical devices, while Grady has successfully navigated the FDA pathway twice (NightWare breakthrough designation and clearance) and knows how to commercialize into VA/DoD markets—exactly what Braillic needs as it scales ArNav and pursues FDA approval. This is a classic CTO-meets-seasoned-medtech-operator dynamic where Grady's 15 years of regulated AI product experience and commercialization playbook directly address Braillic's stated hiring and FDA consulting priorities.
intro_message: Stiven Ding, meet Grady Hannah — he built and FDA-cleared an AI medical device (NightWare) and is now scaling rapid mental health innovations, and your surgical AR navigation platform could benefit from his playbook on regulated software, FDA strategy, and scaling into government markets.
